purpose: This medication is used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections in your urinary tract (like your kidneys) and infections in your abdomen (like your intestines or belly area). It is also used to treat a serious type of lung infection called hospital-acquired pneumonia. Doctors often use it when other antibiotics have not worked or when the bacteria causing the infection are resistant to other treatments.
how_it_works: Ceftolozane is an antibiotic that works by attacking the outer wall of bacteria, essentially breaking it down so the bacteria die. Tazobactam is a helper ingredient that protects the ceftolozane from being destroyed by certain enzymes that some bacteria produce to fight off antibiotics. Together, they make a strong team that can fight bacteria that are harder to treat.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, headache, fever, constipation, diarrhea, and low potassium levels in your blood. Some patients may also notice a rash or mild stomach upset. Let your doctor or pharmacist know if any of these bother you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic, as you may also be allergic to this one. This medicine is given through an IV in a hospital or clinical setting, so medical staff will be watching you closely. If you develop severe diarrhea or notice blood in your stool, tell your healthcare team right away as this could be a sign of a serious gut infection. Kidney function will need to be monitored during treatment, especially if you already have kidney problems.
typical_dosing: This medication is given through an IV (a drip into your vein) by a nurse or healthcare provider — you will not take this one as a pill at home. The usual dose for most infections is 1.5 grams given every 8 hours over about one hour. Your doctor may adjust the dose if you have kidney problems. Treatment usually lasts between 7 to 14 days depending on the type of infection.
